topic: Joint influence recursion and selection-valid path inference for LTV Synthetic-Blips panels. Fix one target unit, finite T and action set, q=1, fixed latent rank, and a finite budget-feasible path class. Conditional on deterministic LTV latent factors and assignments, let every required action-time donor cell grow proportionally to N; impose independent cross-unit sub-Gaussian innovations with bounded fourth moments, separated normalized factor/loading Grams, row-space inclusion and donor exogeneity, diffuse minimum-norm donor weights, p_N/N^(2+delta)->infinity noisy factor covariates, and a positive-definite limiting oracle covariance. Construct a covariate-row-cross-fitted orthogonal recursive SBE-PCR estimator with an explicit computable unit influence array and uniform joint root-N expansion for all target path values. Prove a multivariate Gaussian approximation and uniform consistency of covariance obtained by replaying the fitted recursion on leave-one-out residuals, including off-diagonal donor-reuse terms; then derive simultaneous path bands, an honest maximizing-path set, and the finite-Gaussian local-gap regret law. Consumer: Synthetic Blips' Korean export-insurance/loan schedule and targeting analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The oracle source coefficients can be propagated exactly through the finite backward graph: each blip-node coefficient equals its donor-weighted observed-outcome coefficient minus propagated baseline and later-blip coefficients. This gives Phi_{r,N}^pi=N H_r^pi epsilon_r and Sigma_N=N sum_r H_r H_r' Var(epsilon_r). In the legal T=2 LTV witness with control, time-1 action, and time-2 action cells, the two path errors are (A,A+B-C), yielding Sigma=[[1,1],[1,3]] without cancellation. A separated rank-k spectral projector is differentiable. Row-space augmentation w'Z+xi'(X_i-X_S w), with xi estimated on opposite covariate-row folds and unit leave-out, makes the population derivative in w vanish, suggesting only nuisance-product remainders remain when p_N/N^(2+delta)->infinity. Checks found no collision with Synthetic Interventions scalar CLTs or dynamic softmax inference, and fixed spectral margins avoid projector boundary nonregularity. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniformly that the orthogonalized finite leave-one-out PCR recursion differs from its oracle version by o_P(N^(-1/2)), controlling spectral derivatives and every cross-fitted augmentation product. EARLY KILL TEST: At one rank-one equal-loading donor node with p_N=N^(2+delta), prove the augmented estimator's oracle expansion and influence-coefficient consistency uniformly; pivot if either root-N remainder fails under the stated gap and diffuseness.

open_problems.open_problem: Can covariate-row-cross-fitted orthogonal SBE-PCR admit a uniform joint root-N influence expansion whose replay covariance retains all off-diagonal terms created by donor reuse across recursive nodes and paths?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Synthetic Blips controls recursively propagated PCR errors only in probability, while Synthetic Interventions isolates a scalar estimand under a different growing-time regime. The prior spectral proposal supplies only a one-step delta method, and the self-normalization proposal supplies a scalar random-scale argument. Here an early projector or donor-weight perturbation changes every ancestor path value, and the same primitive innovation can reappear at several nodes. The missing proof must differentiate the full backward graph, establish orthogonality of the cross-fitted row augmentation, control every spectral and nuisance-product remainder uniformly, and preserve repeated innovations when constructing covariance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving an explicit computable unit influence array, a uniform joint asymptotic-linear expansion over the finite path class, a multivariate Gaussian approximation, and uniformly consistent leave-one-unit-out replay covariance equal to the full shared-donor covariance.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from time-varying latent confounding to low-rank blip recursion, then present joint uncertainty quantification as the missing layer for schedule comparison.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Dynamic latent confounding defeats ordinary regime evaluation -> synthetic blips identify path values through low-rank backward recursion -> policy comparison requires a joint influence law and donor-reuse-aware covariance

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a Neyman-orthogonal augmentation and use cross-fitting so first-stage perturbations enter through products of fold-specific errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required SBE expansion likewise needs PCR-weight and row-space-regression errors to interact only at second order.

method_exemplars.technique: Debias a low-rank nuisance using sample splitting, eigenspace rotation, and post-regularization refitting, then prove asymptotic normality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both settings must remove the first-order effect of estimating a separated spectral subspace from a target causal functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate the oracle donor-noise term from PCR weight-estimation error and impose projected-error conditions yielding a scalar Gaussian limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest PCR-based causal-panel CLT, whose scalar decomposition must be propagated through the SBE backward graph.

open_problems.open_problem: Which primitive learner and fold conditions make every covariate-row augmentation product generated by the finite leave-one-out PCR recursion uniformly o_P(N^{-1/2})?

source_refs.excerpt: no primitive learner class, rate derivation, or attainable example discharges it

open_problems.why_unsolved: The reviewed panel argument assumes the nuisance-variation rate needed for its bias-product bound instead of deriving it from a learner. In SBE, pointwise nuisance convergence is insufficient because weight errors, row-regression errors, spectral-projector derivatives, and leave-one-out perturbations are propagated through later blip nodes. The early rank-one witness therefore requires a primitive concentration and stability argument that converts p_N/N^(2+delta) growth and donor diffuseness into uniform second-order remainder bounds.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem for a named cross-fitted learner class proving influence-coefficient consistency and a uniform o_P(N^{-1/2}) bound for every propagated augmentation, spectral, and leave-one-out product remainder, including the rank-one equal-loading witness.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its recursive PCR construction to state precisely which existing consistency remainder must be strengthened to root-N scale.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PCR controls low-rank donor prediction error -> backward blip recursion propagates that error through multiple nodes -> orthogonal cross-fitting must convert all propagated first-stage effects into root-N-negligible products

method_exemplars.technique: Prove orthogonal-score expansions by conditioning on training folds and bounding products of nuisance-estimation errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is a recursive, spectral analogue of the DML product-rate remainder theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Control sample-split eigenspace estimation and post-refitting errors uniformly for linear functionals of a low-rank model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It addresses the spectral-nuisance component that ordinary DML theory leaves abstract.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite budget-feasible menu of dynamic paths evaluated by jointly Gaussian SBE-PCR estimates, what data-dependent set contains every welfare-maximizing path uniformly under root-N local ties, and what is the finite-Gaussian limit of plug-in regret?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Synthetic Blips selects schedules using point estimates, whereas existing confidence-aware policy methods assume a valid joint Gaussian approximation and covariance are already available. Inference on Winners targets the selected coordinate rather than all population maximizers. Under root-N local gaps, max and argmax are nonregular and correlated donor-reuse noise changes the chosen path with nonvanishing probability. The unresolved step is to combine the SBE joint influence law with Gaussian-max critical values and directional analysis of max and set-valued argmax.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving simultaneous path-band coverage, a uniformly honest confidence set for all maximizing paths, and the explicit weak limit of root-N regret as a functional of a correlated finite Gaussian vector shifted by the local path-gap vector.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its Korean export-insurance and loan scheduling application to frame selection as the policy decision rather than an abstract multiple-comparisons problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic blips recover values for feasible support sequences -> agencies choose a budget-feasible schedule from estimated values -> near ties and shared donor noise require an honest maximizing set and local-gap regret law

method_exemplars.technique: Simulate maxima from an estimated joint Gaussian covariance to form simultaneous welfare bounds and confidence-aware policy choices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once SBE supplies its donor-reuse covariance, Gaussian-max inversion directly yields simultaneous path comparisons.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine conditional and projection inference for a coordinate selected from a correlated Gaussian estimate vector.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An estimated SBE-optimal path is the winning coordinate of just such a vector, although coverage must be enlarged to the full maximizer set.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed treatment choice in a local Gaussian experiment and evaluate the induced limiting decision risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested local-gap regret distribution is a finite-action Gaussian decision problem after establishing the SBE joint expansion.

open_problems.open_problem: Can simultaneous SBE path inference remain uniformly valid when the weakest factor and relevant PCR eigengap approach the noise scale and the working rank may overestimate the latent rank?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The fixed-margin SBE argument begins with differentiability of a separated spectral projector, which fails as retained and discarded singular spaces collide. Existing weak-factor and rank-robust methods concern static low-rank functionals. In SBE, projector bias is repeatedly propagated through later-blip subtraction, so transferring those corrections requires a recursive bias envelope and a characterization of how weak factors interact with donor diffuseness and local path comparisons.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A bias-aware simultaneous confidence region for finite SBE path values with coverage uniform over specified weak-factor and rank-overestimation classes, together with a sharp phase-transition condition or counterexample identifying where root-N inference is impossible.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its strong-factor benchmark, weak-factor failure diagnosis, and bias-aware repair, replacing a static panel coefficient with recursive SBE path values.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Factor methods enable tractable panel inference under strong signals -> weak factors make conventional intervals unreliable -> dynamic synthetic-blip recursion needs bias-aware inference as its PCR eigengaps weaken

method_exemplars.technique: Use minimax-linear debiasing and a nuclear-norm bound on unresolved interactive effects to construct bias-aware confidence intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unresolved weak-factor component in SBE also enters target linear functionals, but its bias must be propagated through a backward graph.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate factor spaces with diversified projections and correct the implicit-ridge bias induced by rank overestimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: SBE-PCR likewise applies an estimated low-rank projection before evaluating donor-weighted linear functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Use eigenspace rotation and post-regularization refitting for efficient inference under separated strong factors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the regular strong-factor endpoint that a uniform weak-factor SBE theory should recover.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what coupled growth conditions on horizon, action count, feasible-path cardinality, donor sizes, and spectral margins does recursive SBE-PCR support high-dimensional simultaneous path bands?

open_problems.why_unsolved: A high-dimensional Gaussian theorem becomes applicable only after SBE is represented as a sum of unit influence vectors with controlled coordinate envelopes. As horizon grows, backward recursion can amplify donor-weight norms, spectral derivatives, and nuisance products; donor nesting also changes the minimum effective sample size and can make nearby paths almost perfectly correlated. The missing step is a recursive envelope bound strong enough to offset path-class entropy and Gaussian anti-concentration error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A high-dimensional Gaussian and residual- or multiplier-bootstrap approximation theorem with explicit rate restrictions linking log path-class size, horizon, donor diffuseness, minimum donor count, and spectral gap, yielding honest simultaneous path bands.

writing_exemplar.why: Follow its sample-complexity comparison between sequence-specific interventions and additive blip recursion, then pose inference complexity as the unresolved scaling problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sequence-specific synthetic interventions require exponentially many donor regimes -> additive blip recursion reduces estimation to action-time nodes -> a growing feasible path menu still requires uniform Gaussian theory tracking recursive amplification and menu size

method_exemplars.technique: Apply hyperrectangle Gaussian approximation and multiplier bootstrap to maxima of sums of independent high-dimensional influence vectors using Gaussian anti-concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Simultaneous SBE path bands become hyperrectangle probabilities for a high-dimensional sum once the recursive influence array is constructed.

method_exemplars.technique: Use randomized Lindeberg interpolation to sharpen max-statistic Gaussian and bootstrap approximation rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharper logarithmic and moment dependence directly enlarges the admissible growth rate of the feasible SBE path class.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct uniform synthetic-control prediction inference across multiple post-treatment indices while accounting for estimated weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest synthetic-control-specific uniform inference framework, although SBE indexes estimates by recursive action paths.

literature_map:
Agarwal, Han, Saha, Syrgkanis, and Yoon (2025, arXiv:2210.11003) identify arbitrary dynamic paths by a backward synthetic-blip recursion and prove pointwise PCR consistency, but provide no influence-function or Gaussian inference theory.
Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2024, arXiv:2006.07691) establish a scalar Synthetic Interventions CLT only with a growing post-period, projected weight-error control, and a rank-sized donor subset.
Agarwal, Harris, Whitehouse, and Wu (2023, NeurIPS, arXiv:2307.01357) give time-uniform finite-sample PCR bounds under adaptive collection, not root-N causal inference for recursive path values.
Chernozhukov, Hansen, Liao, and Zhu (2023, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2107.02602) obtain efficient low-rank inference using sample splitting, eigenspace rotation, and post-regularization OLS.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) supply the orthogonal-score and cross-fitting template needed to turn first-stage nuisance errors into product remainders.
Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2021, JASA, arXiv:1811.04170) augment synthetic-control weights with an outcome model to debias imperfect balance, but their construction is static and nonrecursive.
Arkhangelsky et al. (2021, AER, arXiv:1812.09970) prove asymptotic normality for synthetic difference-in-differences under interactive fixed effects, targeting an aggregate one-shot effect rather than path values.
Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2025 revision, arXiv:1812.10820) use cross-fit bias correction and self-normalized t inference for scalar average synthetic-control effects.
Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021, JASA, arXiv:1912.07120) separate weight-estimation and post-treatment prediction uncertainty; Cattaneo et al. (2025, ReStat, arXiv:2210.05026) extend uniform prediction inference to staggered adoption.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2017, Annals of Probability, arXiv:1412.3661), refined by Chernozhukov et al. (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1912.10529), provide Gaussian and bootstrap approximation for maxima with unrestricted coordinate correlation.
Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey (2024, QJE, DOI:10.1093/qje/qjad043) treat winner's-curse inference for a selected coordinate, while Chernozhukov, Lee, Rosen, and Sun (2026, arXiv:2502.10653) assume a joint Gaussian approximation to construct confidence-aware policy rules.
Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica, DOI:10.3982/ECTA6630) use local Gaussian experiments for treatment-choice risk, furnishing machinery for a finite-Gaussian local-gap regret law.
Athey and Wager (2021, Econometrica, arXiv:1702.02896) and Nie, Brunskill, and Wager (2021, JASA, arXiv:1905.09751) prove regret for orthogonal static and dynamic policy scores, but not for pseudo-outcomes sharing recursively fitted donor pools.
Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026, JPE, arXiv:2210.06639) show weak factors invalidate conventional panel inference, while Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2025, arXiv:2311.16440) show rank overestimation creates implicit-ridge bias; neither covers dynamic synthetic-blip recursion.
prior_proposal_map:
The bounded Track-A catalogue contained nine reviewer JSONs and no canonical proto_core.json, rejected-angle archive, proposal.tex, bank README, or discovery/writeup.tex files.
panel_ipcw_spectral_ssc_inference/reviews/review_math.json yielded the closest panel evidence: an underived primitive learner rate and an unresolved one-step spectral delta construction.
That review's joint-spectral-limit finding supplies a technique donor for backward LTV influence propagation, but not the recursive derivative calculation.
exp_bandit_random_qv_studentization_frontier/reviews/review_rubric.json yielded an adjacent early-measurable self-normalization construction and a demand to isolate the new random-scale feature.
scm_selective_label_untrialed_impact/reviews/review_math.json verified Fang--Santos directional delta machinery and Raič convex-set Gaussian approximation for the path-max layer.
exp_rollout_common_uniform_covariance_design/reviews/review_math.json was inspected, but its degree-one budget dependency was too design-specific to anchor an LTV opportunity.
The remaining reviewer JSONs were inspected and did not contain limitations materially tied to recursive spectral panel inference.
